mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening economy, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate revenues and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances with rising RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a supply-side contraction, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 200k, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals accommodative monetary policy with potential inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) also decline, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST declines > 10% and RSAFS also declines, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 3% in a quarter and GDP (GDPC1) also grows, it signals a strong supply-side expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 3% in 3 months and GDPC1 grows
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 3% and GDPC1 grows, the hypothesis is rejected.
